problems.title: Total degree of a product
problems.question: Find the degree of the monomial obtained from (−199p⁶t³)⁵(99pq⁴)³.
problems.idea: Powers multiply each variable exponent; product degrees add.
formulas: First factor degree=5(6+3)=45; second factor degree=3(1+4)=15.
steps: The nonzero numerical coefficient does not affect degree.
Total degree=45+15.

problems.title: A telescoping polynomial product
problems.question: Simplify (x−1)(1+x+x²+⋯+x²⁰).
problems.idea: Distribute x and −1 and cancel the repeated terms.
steps: Every term from x through x²⁰ appears once with each sign.

problems.title: Quadratic terms cancel in an equation
problems.question: Solve (x−5)(x+3)−(x−3)²=6.
problems.idea: Expand both products.
steps: Subtract to get 4x−24=6.

problems.title: Multiply monomials with a mixed-number coefficient
problems.question: Simplify 1 11/25·a⁷b²·(−(5/6)a²b⁷)².
problems.idea: Square the entire second monomial, including its sign and coefficient.
steps: The coefficients multiply to 1.
The exponents add: a^{7+4}b^{2+14}.

problems.title: Complete an identity by comparing a cross term
problems.question: Find k so (a−b)²=(a+b)²+kab is an identity.
problems.idea: Expand both squares.
steps: The ab coefficient must satisfy 2+k=−2.

problems.title: Factor an exponential sum
problems.question: Which listed natural number divides 2¹⁶+2¹⁵+2¹⁴?
problems.idea: Factor out the smallest power.
steps: This contains the factor 7·4=28.
The other listed values 24,25,26,27,29 do not divide it.

problems.title: Subtract a triangle’s exterior-angle relation
problems.question: An exterior angle at A exceeds the interior angle at B by 64°. Find C.
problems.idea: An exterior angle is the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
steps: Subtract B from both sides. The stated difference is C.

problems.title: Reuse two given monomial values
problems.question: 3x³y=4 and x²z³=−3. Find −x⁹z⁹y.
problems.idea: Group the target into the known factors.
steps: x³y=4/3 and (x²z³)³=(−3)³=−27.
The value is −(4/3)(−27).

problems.title: Distances between four parallel lines
problems.question: Four distinct parallel lines a,b,c,d have distances ab=1,bc=3,cd=7. Which listed value can be distance ad?
problems.idea: Represent the lines by coordinates on a perpendicular axis.
steps: Its possible absolute values are 3,5,9,11. Distinctness can be satisfied, for example with a=0,b=−1,c=2,d=9.
Only 9 appears among the listed choices.

problems.title: A sum of two cubes
problems.question: Factor x³+3x²y+3xy²+2y³.
problems.idea: Recognize (x+y)³+y³.
steps: With u=x+y,v=y the factors are x+2y and (x+y)²−y(x+y)+y².
The second factor simplifies to x²+xy+y².

problems.title: A fixed units digit for positive indices
problems.question: Find the last digit of 2^{n+1}3^{n+2} for positive integer n.
problems.idea: Combine matching powers of 2 and 3.
steps: Every positive power of 6 ends in 6.
18·6 ends in 8, so the whole expression does too.

problems.title: Solve a difference-of-squares equation
problems.question: Which listed number solves 9(x−3)²−4(x−1)²=0?
problems.idea: Factor as a difference of squares.
steps: The roots are x=7 and x=11/5.
The listed root is 11/5=2 1/5.
problems.answer: Listed root 2 1/5; the complete solution set is {7,11/5}.

problems.title: Maximize by completing two squares
problems.question: Find the maximum of 69+8xy+6x−y²−25x².
problems.idea: Group a square in y−4x, then complete the remaining x-square.
steps: Both subtracted squares are nonnegative.
They vanish together at x=1/3,y=4/3.

problems.title: An interior and an exterior angle bisector
problems.question: The bisectors of interior angle A and exterior angle B meet at D, with angle ADB=38°. Find C.
problems.idea: Their angle is half the third triangle angle.
steps: For example in triangle ABD, angle A is A/2 and the obtuse angle at B is 90°+B/2, leaving (180°−A−B)/2.
Thus C=2·38°.

problems.title: A square resting on a right triangle’s hypotenuse
problems.question: A square has two vertices on the hypotenuse of an isosceles right triangle and its other two on the legs. Its perimeter is 1⅓. Find the hypotenuse.
problems.idea: Relate the available width at the square’s height to the full triangle width.
formulas: Square side s=(4/3)/4=1/3; triangle altitude to hypotenuse h=c/2.
steps: At height s above the hypotenuse, similarity gives triangle width c(1−s/h)=c−2s.
This width is the square side s. Hence c=3s.

problems.title: A median direction and the right-angle bisector
problems.question: In a right triangle, the angle between the median and bisector from the right vertex is 25°. Find the larger acute angle.
problems.idea: The hypotenuse midpoint has coordinates proportional to the two leg lengths.
formulas: The median makes an angle equal to one acute triangle angle with a leg; the bisector makes 45°.
steps: Thus the acute angles differ from 45° by 25°.
They are 20° and 70°.

problems.title: A median splits unequal perimeter contributions
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base one quarter of a leg. A median splits it into triangles whose perimeters differ by 6 cm. Find a leg.
problems.idea: The common median and the two half-side pieces cancel in the perimeter difference.
formulas: If the leg is a and base a/4, the difference is a−a/4=3a/4.
steps: A median from the apex would give equal perimeters, so the stated median is from a base vertex.
Set 3a/4=6.

problems.title: A parallel line through an incenter
problems.question: AB=4,BC=5,AC=6. A line through the incenter parallel to AC meets AB,BC at M,K. Find perimeter MBK.
problems.idea: Use the height ratio and the inradius.
formulas: Full perimeter P=15; r/h=AC/P=6/15, since area=rP/2=AC·h/2.
steps: The upper triangle BMK has similarity scale (h−r)/h=1−6/15=3/5.
Its perimeter is 15·3/5.

problems.title: A perpendicular hidden in a short side length
problems.question: AB=2, A=60°, B=70°. D lies on AC with AD=1. Find angle DBC.
problems.idea: AD is exactly the projection of AB onto AC.
steps: Therefore BD⊥AC and triangle ABD is right at D.
Angle ABD=30°. Subtract it from angle ABC=70°.

problems.title: A bisector in a 30–60–90 triangle
problems.question: In right triangle MKE, K=90°, E=30°, KE=12. Find bisector MC.
problems.idea: Find the other two sides and use the angle-bisector theorem.
steps: KC+CE=12, so KC=4.
Triangle MKC is right, giving MC²=(4√3)²+4²=64.

problems.title: Leading terms cancel when finding a polynomial degree
problems.question: Find the degree after expanding (4x²y²−x)³−(8x³y³−x)².
problems.idea: Check the leading cancellation, then the next surviving term.
steps: After cancellation the polynomial is −48x⁵y⁴+16x⁴y³+12x⁴y²−x³−x².
The highest surviving total degree is 5+4=9.

problems.title: Group a negative square before factoring
problems.question: Factor x²−y²−4y−4.
problems.idea: The last three terms equal −(y+2)².
steps: Remove the inner parentheses.

problems.title: A constant disguised as a polynomial
problems.question: Evaluate 4(x−3)²−8(x−3)(x+1)+(2x+2)² at x=199.
problems.idea: The entire expression is a square.
steps: The bracket is −8 for every x.
Its square is 64, including at x=199.

problems.title: Apply a cubic difference identity
problems.question: Given x³−y²=2, find x⁹−6x³y²−y⁶.
problems.idea: Set A=x³,B=y².
steps: Since A−B=2, A³−B³=8+6AB.
Subtracting 6AB leaves 8.

problems.title: Count triangles with distinct integer sides
problems.question: How many triangles have three different integer side lengths selected from 2,…,7?
problems.idea: Count unordered triples and exclude those violating the triangle inequality.
formulas: There are C(6,3)=20 triples; for sorted a<b<c, require a+b>c.
steps: There are seven invalid triples, leaving 20−7.
